title: Types of Halogenoalkanes
author: oA7a2DXCeN3DLamvj
chapter_outcomes: Recall the reactions (reagents and conditions) by which halogenoalkanes can be produced; (a) the free-radical substitution of alkanes by $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ or $\mathrm{Br_2}$ in the presence of ultraviolet light, as exemplified by the reactions of ethane, (b) electrophilic addition of an alkene with a halogen, $\mathrm{X_2}$ , or hydrogen halide, HX(g), at room temperature, (c) substitution of an alcohol, e.g. by reaction with HX(g) or with $\mathrm{KCl}$ and concentrated $\mathrm{H_2 SO_4}$ or concentrated $\mathrm{H_3 PO_4}$ or with $\mathrm{PCl_3}$ and heat or with $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ or with $\mathrm{SOCl_2}$
Classify halogenoalkanes into primary, secondary and tertiary

Describe the following nucleophilic substitution reactions; (a) the reaction with $\mathrm{NaOH_{(aq)}}$ and heat to produce an alcohol, (b) the reaction with $\mathrm{KCN}$ in ethanol and heat to produce a nitrile, (c) the reaction with $\mathrm{NH_3}$ in ethanol heated under pressure to produce an amine, (d) the reaction with aqueous silver nitrate in ethanol as a method of identifying the halogen present as exemplified by bromoethane
Describe the elimination reaction with $\mathrm{NaOH}$ in ethanol and heat to produce an alkene as exemplified by bromoethane
Describe the $\mathrm{S_N1}$ and $\mathrm{S_N 2}$ mechanisms of nucleophilic substitution in halogenoalkanes including the inductive effects of alkyl groups

Recall that primary halogenoalkanes tend to react via the $\mathrm{S_N 2}$ mechanism; tertiary halogenoalkanes via the $\mathrm{S_N 1}$ mechanism; and secondary halogenoalkanes by a mixture of the two, depending on structure

Describe and explain the different reactivities of halogenoalkanes (with particular reference to the relative strengths of the C–X bonds as exemplified by the reactions of halogenoalkanes with aqueous silver nitrates)
